From landing her first holiday job at 17 to becoming the Marketing Manager of Communications Fiji Limited and the owner of The Rotisserie, Felisha Hazelman-Tuiloma has built a career shaped by curiosity, resilience and a willingness to embrace new opportunities.

On this week's fijivillage Her-Story with Temalesi Vono, Tuiloma opens up about her journey, the lessons that shaped her career and the challenges of balancing family life, running her own business and leading marketing at one of Fiji’s leading media organisations.

Suspended police officer, partner remanded over child assault
item.description: The suspended police officer and his partner, who are involved in the serious assault of a child captured in a video circulating on social media, have been remanded by the Nasinu Magistrates Court. Saint George Sisi Talei and Tofua Raiyasi are jointly charged with one count of an act intended to cause grievous harm.
item.content:encoded:
The suspended police officer and his partner, who are involved in the serious assault of a child captured in a video circulating on social media, have been remanded by the Nasinu Magistrates Court.

Saint George Sisi Talei and Tofua Raiyasi are jointly charged with one count of an act intended to cause grievous harm.

The two appeared before Magistrate Lice Manulevu and were represented by Legal Aid.

However, prosecution lawyer Simione Seruvatu objected to their bail applications, stating that the matter was domestic in nature and that the accused are the parents of the child.

A Domestic Violence Restraining Order (DVRO) has also been issued against both accused.

Police had earlier confirmed that the child underwent a medical examination and is now in the safe care of a relative.

The matter has been adjourned to 21st October.

Navitalai Naivalurua · 07/10/2026

Emergency water supplies are being transported to Malau, Vanua Levu, and Cikobia as communities continue to face dry conditions and water shortages.

A vessel has departed Suva for Malau before proceeding to Cikobia to deliver the much-needed water supplies.

item.title: Totoya villagers target $200,000 for Secondary School development
item.description: The villages of Totoya came out in numbers today to be part of their annual collection at the FMF Gymnasium, where the funds collected will go towards the development of the Totoya Secondary School which caters for children from the islands. Village Headman Suliasi Tukete says the soli was initially launched by a group of Lauan people with connections to Totoya, who contributed $105,000.
item.content:encoded:
The villages of Totoya came out in numbers today to be part of their annual collection at the FMF Gymnasium, where the funds collected will go towards the development of the Totoya Secondary School which caters for children from the islands.

Village Headman Suliasi Tukete says the soli was initially launched by a group of Lauan people with connections to Totoya, who contributed $105,000.

He says the five mataqali in Totoya will each contribute $20,000, with the committee expecting to collect around $200,000 today.

Tukete says their forefathers began the vision of building a school for their children by planting pine trees some 50 years ago.

He says that vision and dream has since become a reality, following the construction of the school in 2005.
